answer: Across the wander, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. Each key must complete its own sequential work before the economy recognises it, and the work is deliberately unbatchable — no shortcut lets one solution cover two identities. The trellis turns identity creation into a metered resource: honest agents pay once, a sybil farm pays per clone, and the profit evaporates. Through the vertex, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
